newsitem.title: USA: Simpson friend now doubts O.J. innocence.
newsitem.headline: Simpson friend now doubts O.J. innocence.

text.p: O.J. Simpson flunked a lie detector test just after the murder of his ex-wife Nicole and her friend Ronald Goldman and even his own lawyer tried to get him to plead guilty, according to one of his closest associates.

In an interview with Barbara Walters to be shown on Friday on ABC-TV's "20/20" programme, long-time Simpson friend Robert Kardashian said he was devastated by the results of the defence-administered test. "I didn't know what to believe."
But he said Simpson convinced him of his innocence by explaining his failing the test this way: "Every time I heard Nicole's name my heart was pounding. I would get ... emotional."

Trial experts said it was the first time a key figure in the case has directly said Simpson, who was found not guilty of the murders a year ago, had flunked the test. Because of the possibility of error, lie detector tests are not used as evidence in a trial.

Kardashian also said he offered to give police the Louis Vuitton garment bag he had carried from Simpson's house shortly after Simpson returned from Chicago after the murders. But, he said, they were not interested.

There has been speculation that the bag contained evidence. But Kardashian said police never wanted to look at it and when it was turned over to them nine months later, they never performed tests to see if there were any blood spots.
"I don't believe that they really wanted to know the answer," he said, adding he thought police simply wanted the public to speculate that there was something sinister.
Kardashian, a close Simpson friend for 25 years and the man who organised his defence, said he now had doubts about his innocence and their relationship was no longer close.
He also said that key defence lawyer Robert Shapiro thought Simpson was guilty.

"Mr. Shapiro told me one day that he thinks O.J. went over there (his ex-wife's house) and he was just going to poke her tires and she caught him and that's when the murders took place. And I was astounded," he said.
"Here is our lead trial attorney giving me this theory of guilt and I don't want to hear any theories of guilt."

Kardashian said he got into an argument with Shapiro when the lawyer told Simpson he should plea bargain and could receive 12 years in jail. Shapiro also wanted Kardashian named as an accessory to the murders, Kardashian said.

"My jaw dropped," he told Walters, saying he had no idea why Shapiro wanted to name him as an accessory. The result was that Simpson "started yelling at Bob and saying, 'What are you talking about. I don't ever want to hear this again. I didn't do this.'"
"We didn't need our lead attorney having concerns about guilt. Also Johnnie Cochran related better to Mr. Simpson," he said of the man who took over as lead defence lawyer from Shapiro.

Lawrence Shiller, who wrote a book about the case based largely on interviews with Kardashian, told Walters on the same programme Simpson's house was given a complete makeover before the mostly black jury visited it during his trial.

Shiller said pictures of white women were taken off the walls and pictures of black women put up. A nude photograph of Simpson girlfriend Paula Barbieri was removed from Simpson's bedstand and replaced by a picture of his mother.
"I did feel that this was manipulative," Kardashian said.

He also said he had to talk Simpson, who stayed at his home for four nights after the murders, out of committing suicide in a bedroom belonging to Kardashian's daughter. "I said O.J., 'I could never walk in this room. My daughter couldn't sleep in this bed. She'd know what happened here.'"

He added that during the slow-speed car chase shortly before Simpson was arrested, he got a call from Simpson on a portable phone saying, "Bobby, I put a gun to my head and I pulled the trigger and it didn't go off."
